answer.worked:
Use $c^2=a^2+b^2$, then take the positive square root.

Row 1:
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=3^2+4^2\\c^2&=9+16\\c^2&=25\\c&=5\end{align*}$$
Row 2:
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=5^2+12^2\\c^2&=25+144\\c^2&=169\\c&=13\end{align*}$$
Row 3:
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=7^2+24^2\\c^2&=49+576\\c^2&=625\\c&=25\end{align*}$$
Row 4:
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=9^2+40^2\\c^2&=81+1600\\c^2&=1681\\c&=41\end{align*}$$
Row 5:
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=11^2+60^2\\c^2&=121+3600\\c^2&=3721\\c&=61\end{align*}$$
The values of $a$ increase by 2 each row. Each value of $c$ is 1 greater than the corresponding value of $b$.
